i1_processing_purpose: NestWave processes smart home device event logs, geolocation, and behavioral data to train and operate a personalized automation recommendation engine that surfaces tailored device schedules and routines to each consumer. The processing enables the core differentiated value of the NestWave platform.
i1b_min_pi: Only device event logs, hub geolocation, and account identifiers necessary to generate accurate automation recommendations are processed; granular room-level audio or video data is not collected. Aggregated statistics replace individual records wherever model training permits.
i2_retention_detail: Behavioral profile data is deleted within 90 days of account closure; raw event logs are purged on a rolling 12-month basis regardless of account status.
i2_retention_period: Device event logs retained 12 months; profile model data retained for duration of active account relationship.
i4b_sources: Personal information is collected directly from consumers at account registration and through the NestWave mobile app, and automatically from connected smart home hub devices and sensors installed in the consumer's home.
i5_admt_fairness_testing: Vendor-supplied bias summary reviewed at onboarding; internal fairness testing has not yet been independently conducted.
i5_admt_human_review: Product specialists review automation recommendations flagged as anomalous by the confidence-score threshold; they have authority to suppress or modify a recommendation before it is surfaced to the consumer.
i5_admt_logic: The automation recommendation engine uses a gradient-boosted ML classifier trained on anonymized device event logs to identify recurring usage patterns and predict preferred automation schedules. Feature inputs include time-of-day, device state sequences, and geofence entry/exit events.
i5_admt_training_source: Training data consists of pseudonymized historical device event logs collected from opted-in beta users; no third-party data broker datasets are used.
i6_vendors: AWS (cloud hosting and ML inference), Segment (event data pipeline), Stripe (payment processing), and Zendesk (customer support).
i7_external_consultees: Outside privacy counsel (Hogan & Reed LLP) reviewed the notice framework; no external data ethics consultants were formally engaged.
i7_internal_contributors: Product Engineering, Data Science, Privacy & Legal, and Customer Experience teams contributed to the design and ongoing operation of this processing activity.
